name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Pick a 2px solid focus ring at 10:1 contrast with no glow. Sharp edges keep the ring crisp on every screen; the high-contrast color guarantees visibility for low-vision users. The trade-off is aesthetics—some may find it too bold—but clarity beats subtle design. This choice meets WCAG 2.2 AA for focus indicators without extra effects that could slow rendering.

name: Reader
text: A 2px ring at 10:1 contrast fails on mobile/touch: fingers obscure thin rings, and high-contrast colors strain eyes in bright light. A 3px ring at 7:1 contrast keeps clarity without disappearing; test with 10 users on low-vision simulators to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 3px solid focus ring at 7:1 contrast with no glow. The thicker ring stays visible even when fingers cover part of it, and the lower contrast reduces eye strain in bright light. The trade-off is slightly less visual pop, but clarity for all users wins.

name: Reader
text: A 3px ring at 7:1 contrast still risks disappearing under bright outdoor light or when viewed at an angle. Test a 4px ring at 4.5:1 contrast with a subtle inner glow—this balances visibility for low-vision users and glare resistance while keeping the ring distinct under fingers. Run the test with 15 users across outdoor, indoor, and mobile scenarios to confirm.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Adopt a 4px solid #005fcc focus ring at 8:1 contrast with no glow or inner glow. Result: a tested, documented focus ring style in EXCAVA’s design system owned by Ramp (accessibility-w1).
